project:
## Overview

Safe Shield (also called GuptAI by the team; final name is open) is a Chrome Manifest V3 browser extension that protects people using cloud AI with private documents. It detects and redacts sensitive content locally before the user submits a prompt, then lets the user review the redacted version and restore originals locally.

## Problem statement

Hacktoberfest Hack Day, problem statement #3: “PII redaction for Indian documents and languages”. People paste documents containing names, IDs, and account numbers into cloud chatbots. The product helps anyone using cloud AI with private documents.

The slide’s “What to build” box discusses news claims and source verification and appears to belong to a different problem statement. The team follows the PII project description; see D-001.

## Requirements

Core features:

- Automatic PII detection.
- Smart redaction with stable, typed placeholders.
- Pre-submission protection before text leaves the page.
- Privacy shield toggle.
- Detection preview before sending.
- Local restoration of original text.
- Privacy dashboard with counts only.
- Indian language support, including Hindi/Hinglish where feasible.
- Clean, modern UI.

First supported platform: ChatGPT at `chatgpt.com` and `chat.openai.com`.

Delivery is time-boxed to six hours, with feature freeze at about hour 5.5. Tier 1 is must-have, Tier 2 is only if stable, and Tier 3 is after the window.

## Privacy rules

- All detection runs locally.
- Never send unredacted text to any external service.
- Fail closed: if detection or redaction throws, block the send and warn the user.
- Show “Active” only if the composer is found and interception hooks are attached.
- Keep the placeholder-to-original map in memory or `chrome.storage.session` only.
- Persist dashboard counts only, never detected values.
- Gemma is optional Tier 3; prefer local execution (for example, through Ollama), and only provide already-redacted text. The core project requires no model API.

## Tech stack

Chrome Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no bundler, and no runtime dependencies. Development dependencies may support formatting, linting, and tests. Any optional Gemma integration is Tier 3 only.

## Architecture and data flow

`type -> intercept send -> detect locally -> redact -> preview -> send redacted -> update counts`

Content scripts target the ChatGPT composer. Since MV3 content scripts cannot use ES module imports without a bundler, files in `src/core`, `src/shared`, and `src/content` attach exports to `globalThis.SafeShield` and use a guarded `module.exports` for Node tests.

## Contracts

- `detect(text) -> [{ type, start, end, value }]`
- `redact(text) -> { redactedText, entities: [{ placeholder, type, original }], counts }`
- `restore(text, entities) -> string`
- Placeholder form: `[TYPE_n]`, numbered per type; the same value receives the same placeholder.
- Storage keys: `enabled` (boolean) and `stats` (counts per type only).

## Ownership map

- M1: detection engine (`src/core`) and tests.
- M2: platform integration (`src/content`).
- M3: UI/UX (`src/ui`) and assets.
- M4: foundation, data, and docs (`manifest.json`, `src/shared`, `src/dashboard`, `src/background`, `docs`, `.github`, and scripts).

## Conventions

- Branch names: `feat/<member>-<task>`.
- Use conventional commit prefixes such as `feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, and `chore:`.
- Keep pull requests small.
- Review pairing: M1 <-> M2 and M3 <-> M4.
- Keep per-member history in `docs/changelog/member-N.md`; generated master files must not be edited by hand.

## Open questions

- Final product name: “Safe Shield” or “GuptAI”.

decisions.title: Chrome MV3 with plain JavaScript
decisions.body:
**Decision:** Use Chrome Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no bundler, and the `globalThis.SafeShield` namespace with a guarded CommonJS export for tests.
**Why:** MV3 content scripts cannot use ES module imports without a bundler, and the product must run directly from source.
**Alternatives:** Add a bundler or use module imports in content scripts.
**Impact:** Keep source files compatible with direct script loading and Node tests.

decisions.title: Local deterministic detection; optional Gemma later
decisions.body:
**Decision:** Use local regex and checksum detection for the core; consider Gemma only as optional Tier 3 with already-redacted input.
**Why:** Core privacy must not depend on an external model service.
**Alternatives:** Send prompts to a hosted model for detection.
**Impact:** Core operation requires no model API; any optional AI path must enforce redacted-only input.

decisions.title: Per-member logs and generated master files
decisions.body:
**Decision:** Keep append-only per-member logs and generate master changelog/state files.
**Why:** Separate ownership reduces concurrent edit conflicts while preserving a single current handoff.
**Alternatives:** Have all members edit one shared changelog and state file.
**Impact:** Edit `docs/changelog/member-N.md`; never hand-edit generated master files.

latestPerMember.body:
**Prompt:** fix: prevent modal click-through and close popup on send redacted
**What changed:**
- Fixed critical pointer-events bug in `src/ui/overlay/preview-modal.js` and `preview-modal.css`: added `pointer-events: auto` to `.ss-backdrop`, `.ss-modal`, `.ss-close-btn`, and `.ss-btn`, and dynamically toggled `hostEl.style.pointerEvents = 'auto'` while the modal is open. When closed, resets host pointer events to `none`.
- Added pointer event propagation stop (`stopPropagation`, `preventDefault`) on backdrop, mousedown, mouseup, pointerdown, and button clicks, completely preventing clicks from bleeding through to underlying ChatGPT page elements.
- Added 3-second timeout guard to local AI classification calls in `interceptor.js` and `main.js` so offline Ollama service instances never hang or freeze the UI.
- Optimized capture-phase click listener in `interceptor.js` with early bailouts for clicks originating on `#safeshield-preview-modal-host` and non-clickable elements.
**Files:** `src/ui/overlay/preview-modal.js` (modified), `src/ui/overlay/preview-modal.css` (modified), `src/content/interceptor.js` (modified), `src/content/main.js` (modified)
**Status:** done
**Tasks:** T1-08, T1-11
**Decisions:** none
**Notes for others:** The modal buttons now reliably capture mouse clicks and immediately close the dialog upon clicking 'Send redacted', 'Cancel', or 'Restore original' without passing clicks through to ChatGPT.
**Next:** Reload extension at chrome://extensions and test 'Send redacted' on chatgpt.com to verify popup closes promptly.

**Prompt:** fix: copy redacted text to clipboard and paste to composer without auto-send
**What changed:**
- Replaced programmatic button click / Enter submission in `composer.js`, `interceptor.js`, and `main.js` with direct clipboard copy (`navigator.clipboard.writeText`), pasting into the ChatGPT composer (`composer.setText`), and focusing the textarea.
- Removed global `document.execCommand('selectAll')` in favor of element-scoped `Range` selection, eliminating CSP violations with internal sandboxed iframes (such as `runner.html`).
- Displayed user feedback notification (`modal.warnInfo('📋 Redacted text copied to clipboard & pasted into composer.')`) upon Send Redacted confirmation.
- Retained full privacy guarantees: ephemeral vault caching, stats counting, and pre-submit safety checks all continue to run.
**Files:** `src/content/composer.js` (modified), `src/content/interceptor.js` (modified), `src/content/main.js` (modified)
**Status:** done
**Tasks:** T1-08, T1-11
**Decisions:** none
**Notes for others:** Clicking Send Redacted now copies the redacted prompt to the user's clipboard and writes it into ChatGPT's composer without triggering automated submission or CSP errors.
**Next:** Reload the extension in chrome://extensions, refresh ChatGPT, and test clicking Send Redacted.

recentActivity.heading: ## M2-004 | 2026-10-25 10:14 | feat/solo-build
recentActivity.body:
**Prompt:** fix: wire Gemma AI Assist into SS_SEND_REDACTED handler in main.js
**What changed:**
- The SS_SEND_REDACTED handler in main.js was calling redactor.redact() directly and then immediately writing to the composer and showing the modal, completely bypassing the Gemma classify step that interceptor.js already implements.
- Replaced the synchronous write-and-show block with an async IIFE that: reads aiAssist from storage, checks word count (≥3) and hasRemainingStructuredPII guard, sends SS_AI_CLASSIFY to the service worker if conditions pass, merges NAME/ADDRESS spans from the response into redactedText and entities, then writes the fully-enriched redacted text to the composer before showing the modal.
- Gemma failure (timeout, unavailable, disabled) is silently swallowed; regex-only redaction result is used as fallback — never blocks the flow.
**Files:** `src/content/main.js` (modified)
**Status:** done
**Tasks:** T3-01
**Decisions:** none
**Notes for others:** The interceptor.js path (Enter key / direct send) already had the Gemma wiring. This fix brings the popup Send Redacted button path to parity. Both paths now mirror each other for AI Assist.
**Next:** Test end-to-end in Chrome — paste prompt with name+address, enable AI toggle, click Send Redacted, confirm NAME_1 and ADDRESS_1 appear in the preview modal.

recentActivity.body:
**Prompt:** fix: handle invalidated extension storage contexts
**What changed:**
- Hardened storage `onChange()` registration and cleanup against stale extension contexts after an extension reload.
- Made `getAiAssist()` return the safe disabled value when its old context is invalidated instead of producing an uncaught error.
- Added an issue note documenting the reload/refresh workflow.
**Files:** `src/shared/storage.js` (modified), `docs/state/issues.md` (modified)
**Status:** in review
**Tasks:** T3-01, T2-04
**Decisions:** none
**Notes for others:** The screenshot error is caused by an old ChatGPT content script surviving an extension reload. The fix prevents storage listener errors; users should still refresh ChatGPT after reloading the extension.
**Next:** Reload SafeShield and refresh ChatGPT, then retest address paste and the warning banner.

recentActivity.heading: ## M1-005 | 2026-10-25 06:46 | main
recentActivity.body:
**Prompt:** feat: warn on AI-detected address paste
**What changed:**
- Added a shared Gemma message helper in the interceptor.
- Extended the capture-phase paste handler to run deterministic redaction first, then classify address/name content with local Gemma when AI Assist is enabled.
- AI-detected address/name pastes now show the same sensitive-data warning banner as phone/PAN/email pastes.
- Added regression coverage for an AI-detected address paste warning.
**Files:** `src/content/interceptor.js` (modified), `tests/qa-behaviour.test.js` (modified)
**Status:** in review
**Tasks:** T3-01, T2-04
**Decisions:** none
**Notes for others:** Paste warning is asynchronous for AI-only entities and appears after the local model responds. It does not block paste; the send-time preview remains the final redaction gate.
**Next:** Reload the extension and ChatGPT tab, enable Local AI Assist, and paste a fake address to verify the warning banner.

openHandoffs.notes: The modal buttons now reliably capture mouse clicks and immediately close the dialog upon clicking 'Send redacted', 'Cancel', or 'Restore original' without passing clicks through to ChatGPT.
Clicking Send Redacted now copies the redacted prompt to the user's clipboard and writes it into ChatGPT's composer without triggering automated submission or CSP errors.
Reload the unpacked extension in chrome://extensions and refresh the active ChatGPT tab before testing.
Post-paste input fallback now actively listens on composerEl for insertFromPaste/insertFromPasteAsQuotation.
The interceptor.js path (Enter key / direct send) already had the Gemma wiring. This fix brings the popup Send Redacted button path to parity. Both paths now mirror each other for AI Assist.
Use `npm test` to run the existing automated tests; there is no `tools/eval/run-eval.js` evaluation runner in this checkout.
The address detector and redactor are verified independently. Reload the extension and open a new ChatGPT tab before testing.
The verified fallback detects `42 Green Park Lane, Pune` as one `ADDRESS` span. Reload the extension and ChatGPT before live testing.
Regex warnings remain synchronous and Gemma is only attempted when regex finds no entities. Reload both the extension and ChatGPT before testing.
Regex-detected phone/PAN/email/Aadhaar data now warns without waiting for Gemma. Address/name warnings still require Gemma when regex cannot identify them.
The supplied attachment was a source snapshot, not a stack trace. A fresh ChatGPT tab is still needed after reloading the extension.
Reloading the unpacked extension still requires refreshing existing ChatGPT tabs; stale content scripts cannot be revived.
This addresses the screenshot at `storage.js` line 192. A fresh ChatGPT tab is still required after reloading the extension because old content scripts cannot be revived.

The screenshot error is caused by an old ChatGPT content script surviving an extension reload. The fix prevents storage listener errors; users should still refresh ChatGPT after reloading the extension.
Paste warning is asynchronous for AI-only entities and appears after the local model responds. It does not block paste; the send-time preview remains the final redaction gate.
Reload both the extension and ChatGPT tab after changing the service worker. Structured phone/PAN detection remains independent of Gemma.

Local smoke classification returned an ADDRESS span from `gemma4:e2b`. Reload the unpacked extension after this change; phone/PAN should use the regex preview immediately even when AI Assist is enabled. Address-only prompts still require Ollama at `127.0.0.1:11434`.

Address classification still requires a running local Ollama instance with the configured model. This machine has no `ollama` executable, so live address detection could not be exercised here. The existing design intentionally falls back to regex-only detection when Gemma is unavailable.
All staged changes are being kept together on `feat/solo-build`; repository guidance prohibits committing directly to `main`.

T1-16 (README, demo script, and test prompts) is now substantially complete. Demo script and test-prompts docs already exist at docs/demo-script.md and docs/test-prompts.md; those may need polish but are not placeholders.
Verhoeff is intentionally dropped from detection — over-redacting is safer than missing a real Aadhaar. If stricter precision is needed later, add it as an opt-in setting, not a default gate.

The SS_SEND_REDACTED handler does NOT run the full fail-closed interceptor path (no final PII re-check before submit). M2 should add a final detect() safety guard before composer.submit if time allows.

Content script (main.js / interceptor.js, owned by M2) must handle the SS_SEND_REDACTED message type and reply with {ok:true}, {ok:false, reason:'no_pii'}, {ok:false, reason:'disabled'}, or {ok:false, message:'...'} for the popup feedback to work end-to-end.
Open a PR from `chore/project-state-handoff` into `main`. Do not merge from this session. Replace CODEOWNERS placeholders with real GitHub usernames.
Generated project state is not hand-edited. Continue to log work by appending entries and regenerating state.
`node_modules/` is ignored; the app has no runtime dependencies and no bundler.
